## Exchanging a SailPoint ISC PAT for an Access Token

This is a standard **OAuth2 client credentials grant**. Send the client ID and secret in the **POST body** (never in the URL/query string).

### curl

```bash
curl -X POST "https://{tenant}.api.identitynow.com/oauth/token" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded" \
  -d "grant_type=client_credentials" \
  -d "client_id=YOUR_CLIENT_ID" \
  -d "client_secret=YOUR_CLIENT_SECRET"
```

### Python (requests)

```python
import requests

tenant = "your-tenant"
url = f"https://{tenant}.api.identitynow.com/oauth/token"

response = requests.post(url, data={
    "grant_type": "client_credentials",
    "client_id": "YOUR_CLIENT_ID",
    "client_secret": "YOUR_CLIENT_SECRET",
})
response.raise_for_status()
access_token = response.json()["access_token"]
```

### Using the token

Pass the returned token as a bearer on every subsequent request:

```
Authorization: Bearer <access_token>
```

> **Note for beta endpoints:** also include `X-SailPoint-Experimental: true`.

### Key details

| Detail | Value |
|---|---|
| Token endpoint | `POST /oauth/token` |
| Content-Type | `application/x-www-form-urlencoded` |
| `grant_type` | `client_credentials` |
| PAT cap | 10 PATs per user |
| Rate limit | 100 requests / token / 10 seconds |
| On 429 | Respect the `Retry-After` response header |

---
